subject.title: Feature Request: Extract text from document attachments in Telegram channel

question: Which Office-document extraction boundary should OpenClaw support for Telegram/shared attachments: native bundled parsing, an external ClawHub/MCP path, or provider-native forwarding instead?
rationale: The remaining capability requires maintainer intent on untrusted parser dependencies, archive/XML limits, MIME scope, and whether this belongs in the bundled document-extract plugin or outside core.

options.title: Bounded shared extractor
options.body: Approve a narrow document-extract plugin path for selected Office MIME types with strict size/inflation limits, MIME sniffing, untrusted-content wrapping, Telegram coverage, and docs.

options.title: External package first
options.body: Keep Office extraction outside core for now and document a ClawHub/MCP companion until security and dependency ownership are settled.

options.title: Defer to native forwarding
options.body: Treat this as part of the broader provider-native file/document forwarding design rather than adding local Office text extraction.

recommendation.title: Bounded shared extractor
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow document-extract plugin path for selected Office MIME types with strict size/inflation limits, MIME sniffing, untrusted-content wrapping, Telegram coverage, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: The central decision sits on the shared document-extractor and input_file seams where this history is strongest.
